_comment: Instance data for core/helpers/time-gate.cjs: regex strings in the operator's own language, merged into the
English built-ins (the built-ins already know 'yesterday', 'last week', 'n days ago', 'recently', 'this morning',
'earlier today', estimated durations such as 'will take about 5 minutes', and the clock slots 'this afternoon',
'this evening', 'tonight'). A brain whose operator writes in another language and leaves these lists empty has a
gate that records nothing in that language.
patterns = past-relative time references (a claim about a timestamp); duration_patterns = an ESTIMATED duration
(future or present tense; a measured 'took 34 s' must not match); dayparts = [{pattern, start}] a slot of today
that starts at hour <start> - the clock mode blocks it while the clock is before <start>, the sentence carries a
past_markers hit and neither a future_markers nor an other_day hit.
local_time_only = true makes the clock mode also hold a clock time tagged UTC/Z in prose (the operator wants
Example for a German operator: patterns "\\bgestern\\b", "\\bvor\\s+\\d+\\s+(tagen|stunden)\\b"; dayparts
_cases: the operator's real wording with the verdict the blocking mode must reach (text = the reply);
run by core/scripts/pattern-cases.py at every self-test.
